title: How to enlarge cursor in VS Code on Mac: a guide for better visibility
metaTitle: How to enlarge cursor in VS Code on Mac
description: Learn how to enlarge cursor on mac in VS Code. Follow these steps to adjust your cursor width and style for better visibility while coding on macOS.
targetKeyword: how to enlarge cursor on mac
intro: You can enlarge the cursor in VS Code on your Mac by adjusting the editor settings for width and style. This simple configuration change helps you track your position more easily while writing code.
tldr: Search for cursor in the top bar.
Adjust Editor: Cursor Width to a higher value.
Change Editor: Cursor Style to block for a larger appearance.

blocks.text: The default cursor in VS Code is a thin vertical line. On high resolution Retina displays, this line can be difficult to spot. Increasing the width or changing the style to a block makes it much clearer. This is a common adjustment for developers who spend long hours in front of the screen. It reduces eye strain and helps maintain focus. You do not need to install extra plugins to achieve this. The functionality is built into the core settings of the editor.
Steps to enlarge cursor on Mac
You can change these settings using the graphical interface. Follow these steps to modify your cursor appearance.

items: Open VS Code on your Mac.
Press ⌘ + , to open the Settings tab.
Type cursor into the search bar.
Locate Editor: Cursor Width and enter a value like 5.
Locate Editor: Cursor Style and select block or block-outline.
Close the settings tab to apply changes.

blocks.text: Advanced users often prefer editing the configuration file directly. This method is faster if you already know the setting names. Open the Command Palette with ⌘ + ⇧ + P and type Open User Settings (JSON). Add the following lines to your object to set your preferences.

Sometimes the cursor behavior changes unexpectedly. If your cursor suddenly replaces text instead of inserting it, you are in Overwrite mode. Look at the status bar at the bottom right of the window. You might see OVR. Click it to return to INS mode. If you use the Vim extension, it may override your custom settings. Check your extension list if the cursor does not behave as expected.

Visual accessibility is a major factor in developer productivity. Studies show that a significant portion of users benefit from high contrast or larger UI elements. Adjusting your cursor is just one way to make your environment more comfortable. You might also consider changing your font size or color theme. Check our guides on how to change the editor font size or how to change the color theme for more ways to customize your workspace.

faq.question: Can I make the cursor blink slower?
faq.answer: Yes. Search for Editor: Cursor Blinking in settings. You can choose options like smooth or expand to change the animation style.

faq.question: Does this work on the web version of VS Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The settings architecture for VS Code for the Web is identical to the desktop version.

steps.text: Select your preferred width and style from the dropdown menus or text fields.
steps.tip: A width of 5 is often enough to make the line cursor much more visible.

troubleshooting.fix: Click OVR in the status bar to switch back to INS mode.
Ensure you are not using an extension like Vim that overrides default cursor behavior.
